title: Fix StudyDayConfigMerger to use DriftMergeStore.remoteIsNewer instead of the pre-Phase-3 merge_rules.remoteIsNewer
rule: FB-2 (server-timestamp / clock-skew LWW ordering, never client-clock-only)
why: Every other LWW merger in this batch (bookmark, track_config, settings, stage_definition, learning_order, profile_program, goal, learner_profile, gamification_settings, notification_settings, ui_preferences — 11 of 12 natural-key/singleton mergers) was upgraded in the documented 'Phase 3' pass to call `_store.remoteIsNewer`, which adds the ±5s clock-skew window plus Firestore server-timestamp (synced_at) tie-break specifically to fix FB-2's 'faster clock always wins' problem (see drift_merge_store.dart:34-38, 111-152, including the D15 fix). StudyDayConfigMerger alone still calls the plain free function from merge_rules.dart, which has neither: it is a strict `remoteUpdatedAt.isAfter(localUpdatedAt)` with no skew tolerance and no server-timestamp fallback. A device whose clock runs even a few seconds fast will have its study-day-config edits always win the comparison, silently discarding a genuinely newer edit made on a second device.
recommendation: Give StudyDayConfigMerger a MergeStore dependency (constructor param, like every sibling merger) and call store.remoteIsNewer with the row's synced_at; drop its import of merge_rules.dart.
acceptance_criteria: Unit test: two devices' clocks 3s apart, both writes inside the ±5s window, no synced_at on one side — StudyDayConfigMerger resolves identically to DriftMergeStoreTest's D15 clock-skew group, not via strict remote.isAfter(local).
grep confirms study_day_config_merger.dart no longer imports the free-function remoteIsNewer from merge_rules.dart.
